key_insight: Pythia autonomously optimizes clinical symptom extraction prompts without manual tuning, achieving strong specificity and solid sensitivity on local clinical notes.
engineering_relevance: This shows a practical path to deployable, privacy-preserving clinical NLP that avoids fine-tuning while outperforming a lexicon on false-positive control.
method: Multi-agent system writes and iteratively optimizes extraction prompts for each symptom concept.
Runs on a locally hosted open-weights model to keep clinical notes on-premises.
Selects prompts using development-set sensitivity and specificity, then validates on held-out notes.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 400 clinical notes from 387 patients across 72 signs and symptoms, with separate development (n=300) and validation (n=100) splits per concept; mean validation sensitivity/specificity were 0.76/0.95.
watch_item: Sensitivity transfer weakened for very rare concepts, especially below 5% prevalence, so low-prevalence symptoms may still need additional safeguards or review.
paper_title: A Multi-Agent System for Autonomous, Fine-Tuning-Free Clinical Symptom Detection: Development and Validation Study
